study_identification_part.si_4_title: Brain charts for the human lifespan

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS) were used for normative trajectories, with site- and study-specific batch effects accounted for and sex-stratified models.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We created brain charts for the human lifespan using generalized additive models for location, scale and shape 2,24 (GAMLSS), a robust and flexible framework for modelling non-linear growth trajectories recommended by the World Health Organization 24 .; Normative brain-volume trajectories were estimated using GAMLSS, accounting for site- and study-specific batch effects, and stratified by sex (female, red; male, blue).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Mapping normative brain growth; Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Fig. 1 | Human brain charts

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Modeled phenotypes include total cortical GMV, WMV, subcortical GMV, ventricular CSF volume, mean cortical thickness, total surface area, and regional cortical volumes (34 cortical areas).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: GAMLSS models were fitted to structural MRI data from control subjects for the four main tissue volumes of the cerebrum (total cortical grey matter volume (GMV), total white matter volume (WMV), total subcortical grey matter volume (sGMV) and total ventricular cerebrospinal fluid volume (ventricles or CSF)).; we generalized the same GAMLSS modelling approach to estimate normative trajectories for additional MRI phenotypes including other morphometric properties at a global scale (mean cortical thickness and total surface area) and regional volume at each of 34 cortical areas
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Mapping normative brain growth; Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Mapping normative brain growth

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Models included age (sex-stratified), sex, site/study effects (batch effects or study indicators), and preprocessing pipeline/software version.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: GAMLSS modelling was used to estimate the relationship between (global) MRI phenotypes and age, stratified by sex, and controlling for technical and other sources of variation between scanning sites and primary studies.; age, preprocessing pipeline and study were each included in the GAMLSS model estimation of first order ( μ ) and second order ( σ ) distribution parameters of a generalized gamma distribution using fractional polynomials to model nonlinear trends.
